title: Asynchronous Inventory Synchronization
business: E-commerce platforms managing high-volume inventory updates across distributed microservices.
problem: Synchronous API calls between the Order Service and the Inventory Service cause request timeouts and cascading failures when the Inventory Service experiences latency spikes during peak traffic.
solution: Cloud Tasks decouples the services by offloading inventory update requests into a managed queue, allowing the Order Service to return an immediate success response while the Inventory Service processes updates at its own pace with built-in retry logic.
steps: Define a Cloud Tasks queue to act as the buffer between the Order and Inventory services.
Configure the target HTTP endpoint on the Inventory Service to receive task payloads.
Modify the Order Service to create a task containing the inventory update details instead of calling the Inventory API directly.
Set retry parameters on the queue to handle transient failures during inventory updates.
Monitor the queue depth and task execution status to ensure consistency.
outcome: Improved system resilience and reduced latency for end-users, as the Order Service is no longer blocked by downstream inventory processing delays.
limitation: Cloud Tasks introduces eventual consistency; check the queue status or task logs to verify if a specific update has been successfully processed or if it has exhausted its retry limit.

questions.question: In Asynchronous Inventory Synchronization, why is Cloud Tasks used?
options: To eliminate the need for an Inventory Service
To prevent Order Service timeouts caused by downstream latency
To increase the processing speed of the Order Service database
To replace the need for HTTP targets
questions.explanation: The scenario identifies that synchronous calls cause timeouts, and the solution uses Cloud Tasks to decouple services to avoid this.

questions.question: In Asynchronous Inventory Synchronization, what is a key trade-off of the implementation?
options: The system becomes strictly consistent immediately
The Order Service must wait for the Inventory Service to finish
The system operates with eventual consistency
Retry logic is not supported for HTTP targets
questions.explanation: Asynchronous processing inherently means the system is eventually consistent, requiring verification of task status.
